request.symptom: low suction pressure and the compressor is short cycling on the low pressure switch

response.body:
Low suction pressure on a Carrier 48LC unit (associated with Alert T133) is typically caused by restricted indoor airflow, excessively cold return air/economizer fault, or liquid line/refrigerant circuit restrictions.

1. Inspect the air filters for excessive dirt and restriction.
   Reading: Visual filter condition and cleanliness. Dirty air filters causing low airflow and reduced evaporating pressure.

2. Inspect the evaporator fan belt tension, belt condition, and fan rotation direction.
   Reading: Fan belt tension/integrity and correct motor rotation. Insufficient evaporator airflow caused by a loose/broken belt or reverse fan rotation.

3. Measure conditioned space return air temperature and check the economizer damper position.
   Reading: Return air temperature and visual economizer damper position. Excessively cold return air or a stuck-open economizer during low ambient outdoor temperatures.

4. Measure operating suction and discharge pressures, calculate superheat and subcooling, and check temperature drop across the liquid line filter drier. Follow standard refrigerant safety procedures when attaching service gauges.
   Reading: Suction pressure, superheat, subcooling, and liquid line temperature drop across the filter drier. Low refrigerant charge, plugged filter drier, or faulty TXV.

Dirty air filters. Replace filters.
Low refrigerant charge. Check pressure, locate leak, repair, evacuate, and
recharge.
Condenser coil dirty or restricted. Clean coil or remove restriction.
Excessive Condenser Pressures. Loose condenser thermistors. Tighten thermistors.
Dirty condenser coil. Clean coil.
Refrigerant overcharge. Recover excess refrigerant.
Faulty TXV. 1. Check TXV bulb mounting and secure tightly to
suction line and insulate.
